issues.location: Opening line, quoted modèles
issues.evidence: The complete word has m/o/d/e/l/e/s contours. A separate short nearly horizontal accent is certainly present above the first e, excluding the unaccented candidate; its polarity remains weak. Both quotation pairs consist of two separate short strokes, not guillemets.

issues.location: (i), final word
issues.evidence: The repeated low monomor arches, descending p, tall h, dotted i, descending q and terminal ue can be followed in half a; the word is not physically unreadable.

issues.location: (ii), cancelled word beneath end
issues.evidence: A short a/u/t/o/m sequence occupies the crossed space. There are no further letter bodies for orphisme. The terminal dark nub touches the cancellation rule, so an independent abbreviation stop cannot be established or excluded.

issues.location: (ii), raised replacement end
issues.evidence: Raised e-n-d appears directly above the crossed abbreviation. The last d has an oval and upright with a rightward exit; the space after that exit is clear and has no separate stop.

issues.location: Example, word after définie
issues.evidence: The crop shows the long descending and returning p, a reduced separate middle stroke, and the final small bent r before the spaced un. This is sufficient to read par without an in-place doubt.

issues.location: Definition of tilde D, first sous objets
issues.evidence: There is a blank gap between sous and objets. It lacks the short horizontal stroke that is visibly present at the later occurrence.

issues.location: Definition of tilde D, quoted inclusion
issues.evidence: Each flank of inclusion is a pair of short detached ticks. No angular guillemet is drawn.

issues.location: End of identification sentence, final tilde D
issues.evidence: The interlinear D with separate tilde ends the sentence spatially; there is no independent full stop to its right. The nearby point above-left belongs to the earlier D sentence, not this endpoint.

issues.location: Starred Hom application display
issues.C: Two rows, M directly below Hom, no comma after tilde D
issues.H: One row with Hom_M, comma after tilde D, followed by u mapsto
issues.evidence: Hom and its lower M are vertically separated. The object arrow is on the upper row and the u mapsto row lies below; the lower arrow begins with a vertical bar. The target D has a separate tilde and no trailing comma. The (*) label sits at the left.

issues.location: First citation after injective par
issues.evidence: The first left enclosure is curved/slanted with a low inward turn; its right enclosure has an especially clear leftward horizontal top and a lower foot, producing a bracket-like right side. A literal mixed (i] is therefore retained ahead of the two conventional alternatives. The following (ii) has two dots and rounded enclosing strokes.

issues.location: Central paragraph, l’ens before cancelled word
issues.evidence: The s ends with its own descending hook. The intervening space before the small crossed word contains no separate abbreviation point.

issues.location: Central paragraph, small crossed word after l’ens
issues.evidence: A compact loop, a possible ascending start and a short e-like lower exit remain visible through the cancellation. They support de, but the overlapping dark strokes do not settle both letters. The C doubt is retained, not silently resolved.

issues.location: Central subset name
issues.evidence: Half b shows a closed upper oval divided by a full central upright which continues to a wide horizontal foot. The two-sided oval is distinct from a one-sided script-L loop. The subscript is D followed by a separate prime. This resolves the alphabet as Phi on this page alone.

issues.location: M- insertion immediately before isomorphes
issues.evidence: The M has an explicit short hyphen to its right. A long curved attachment descends from just after that hyphen to the space immediately before the i of isomorphes. It does not terminate at the subset letter. H has the correct lexical prefix but does not mark its added state.

issues.location: Lower definition, live N after Soit
issues.evidence: The live N has one left upright, one descending diagonal and one returning right upright. There is no separate inner returning stem such as appears in the later N forms.

issues.location: Lower definition, cancelled letter after live N
issues.evidence: The crop separates an upright joining full top and bottom horizontal serifs from the diagonal zigzag cancellation. The I skeleton is continuous; apparent K arms belong to the zigzag.

issues.location: Lower definition, l’ens before préordonné
issues.evidence: The visible abbreviation ends in its low final hook without a detached dot before des/the interlinear addition.

issues.location: Interlinear préordonné
issues.evidence: Préordonné is written above the gap after l’ens; its long bent attachment enters the gap before des. There are no pair of round parentheses enclosing the word.

issues.location: Lower definition, classes
issues.evidence: The crop shows open c, tall looped l, the small a body at its foot, low repeated medial bends, and the long terminal es exit. These establish classes despite the fast reduced ending.

issues.location: End of lower defining sentence, M followed by a point
issues.evidence: A detached low dark point is visible to the right of the M, before the interlinear sentence attaches. It is separate from the right stem of M.

issues.location: Long interlinear sentence, including grâce
issues.H: \note{il est en fait ordonné, grâce à (ii) — l’incise est interlinéaire}
issues.evidence: Half b permits the complete Il est en fait ordonné, grâce à (ii). The g has a descending return, followed by r and the accented middle body, then the short ce exit. A separate straight line under ordonné is deliberate underlining. The large curving line attaches the whole insertion to the point after M. H describes it in an editorial note but does not transcribe it as an insertion or preserve the underline.

issues.location: After Pour, quantifier-shaped glyph
issues.evidence: There are two near-uprights, a horizontal crossbar and a continuous rising diagonal joining the lower left to the upper right. The right upright also continues down below the crossbar. The extra continuation leaves the forall/H identity unresolved; no mathematical expectation was used to remove the alternative.

issues.location: First membership N in Pour n in N
issues.evidence: Half b shows a separate inner returning stroke and projecting bars in the N after membership, unlike the plain N after Soit. The doubled form is resolved at this occurrence.

issues.location: Cancelled ending of un before objet
issues.evidence: The lower surviving letter body has a small enclosed counter followed by a rightward exit, forming e. The taller upper loop and crossing diagonals are the cancellation strokes. There is no separate surviving s contour comparable to the final s elsewhere.

issues.location: After D_n de, overwritten D and live M
issues.evidence: The older broad D bowl and baseline remain beneath the two peaked strokes of a live M. The live letter is retained, and the readable underlying D is recorded before it. H both names the crossed letter differently and loses the replacement.

issues.location: Small mark immediately above classe n
issues.evidence: The mark is a compact crossed cluster with more than one short upper projection and a lower-left foot. It is not a single detached slanted prime. It sits directly above n, not to the upper right. Asterisk is a typographic approximation of this small crossed form.

issues.location: First à isom unique près, abbreviation after déterminé
issues.evidence: The final low m stroke is followed by a line break; there is no independent abbreviation point. The next line starts unique.

issues.location: After unique près, accented/colon-like cluster and detached low stroke
issues.evidence: Two small vertically separated oblique ticks occupy the place read as à in C. No open a bowl survives, so colon remains an ink alternative. A third, distinctly longer down-right stroke sits lower and to the right in the gap before cause; it is preserved as a small lowered backslash without assigning a mathematical role. The three marks are not three equal round dots.

issues.location: Words following the uncertain à/colon-like cluster
issues.evidence: The first word has open c, a closed a, a low u and short terminal se. The following word is the short d-e sequence visible in half b, not the longer dans. The repeated (ii) has two dotted uprights.

issues.location: Lower line, l’ens ordonné before equation
issues.evidence: The abbreviated ens ends in a low horizontal exit; no separate stop appears before ordonné.

issues.location: Equation tilde D_n = J_n
issues.evidence: The full right letter has separated returning stems/white channels, a long top bar and a curved bottom that returns to the left and rises into a hook. These are doubled J contours, rather than a plain I with a straight bottom serif. The lower n is visible to its right; the equality has two separate bars.

issues.location: Lower line, défini
issues.evidence: Half b shows the initial d, the separate acute stroke, a long descending f, dotted i, reduced n and final i. The letters are joined but recoverable.

issues.location: Second à isom unique près, after défini
issues.evidence: The last m exits into the blank at the right of the row. There is no independent stop before the next row unique près. The actual period follows près.

issues.location: Cancelled words before live une famille
issues.evidence: The first crossed word begins with a long descender and a tall looped l; this excludes choisi. Its small later bodies remain merged into the rule, so plus is retained as a doubtful reading. A low comma-like nub follows. The old une is readable under the same deletion line, and a second une is clearly raised above it. The rule reaches the initial f but does not cancel the following whole famille.

issues.location: Final prose line before displayed family, famille
issues.evidence: Half b shows the full descending f, following a/m/i bodies, two tall l strokes and the rightward final e. The cancellation from the earlier words is not a cancellation of famille.

issues.location: Displayed family
issues.evidence: The main family letter has a top bar, separated descending strokes and a distinct leftward rising bottom hook, agreeing with doubled J on its own ink. No D bowl or tilde is present. The family is on its own line, with n in doubled N written as the lower indexing group.

issues.location: Final line, d’ens
issues.evidence: No independent dot follows ens; ordonnés follows after a space. The comma is after ordonnés.

issues.location: Final line, indexés
issues.evidence: The i dot, ascending d, crossed x, short accented e and terminal s hook can be distinguished in half b. The word is indexés, including the final s.

notes: Observation only: this page states two conditions on a category M, gives the ordered-set example, defines the ordered collection of subobjects of D, and states an injectivity/image description for the displayed application. No proof was checked in this run.

Observation only: the lower text introduces isomorphism classes, inserts the assertion “Il est en fait ordonné, grâce à (ii).”, and states uniqueness up to unique isomorphism and a family of ordered sets. These manuscript claims are reported, not independently certified.
Manuscript folio 1 is at top centre; the archive sheet number is 6 at bottom left. There is no date or separate title visible.

No explicit author doubt is written in words on this page. The uncertain marks in reading.tex are reader doubts. Readable deletions, replacements and both substantial interlinear additions are preserved.
Entirely handwritten text sheet. No readable typewriter/print or recoverable reused-sheet text is visible; pale background traces were not reconstructed.
The first N after Soit is plain. Later N occurrences and both J forms were inspected individually for doubled strokes. No alphabet was imported from a different scan.
The complete M- addition is attached to isomorphes by its curved leader. Its position under the subset symbol does not make it a subscript.

The small down-right stroke below the gap after the uncertain à is transcribed as a lowered backslash purely as a typographic approximation. No mathematical function or relation to the nearby two ticks is asserted.
No diagram, ordinary geometric drawing, sideways note or separate marginal prose appears. The isolated short oblique stroke is inventoried separately as a small graphic mark.

The original C_context packet included one row primarily labelled scan 8. It was ignored from the outset, and the parent subsequently confirmed that it had been removed. Historical comparisons with scan 6 were treated only as witness assertions; no other scan was opened.

Initial reads attempted the packet/source paths with an unnecessary SP48_CW_104 prefix and returned file-not-found errors; the correct authorized paths were then used. Those errors delivered no image. Every successful image delivery was viewed once. There were no image-delivery retries.

The final reading was compared once as text against C after image work. Every substantive edit in that comparison has an issue entry, including removals/refinements of C uncertainty. No LaTeX compile or rendering was performed.
